approach: Derive the AB tension from the pulley's force balance, then test unequal masses to see whether it always stays between m₁g and m₂g.

steps.text: For the Atwood pair m₁, m₂ over the frictionless pulley, the common tension in the main string is the standard result.
The pulley itself does not accelerate, since it is held by string AB, so AB must support both downward pulls of T from the two sides of the main string.
Test this with m₁ = 1 kg and m₂ = 1.1 kg.
Compare this with the claimed range from m₁g to m₂g.
T(AB) ≈ 2.095g N is larger than even the bigger weight m₂g = 1.1g N, so it does not lie between m₁g and m₂g here; one such case is enough to make the general 'always' claim false.
The Reason, on its own, is a standard true fact: for an ideal massless string over a frictionless pulley, the tension is the same throughout.

final_answer.value: If the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming T(AB) must be some in-between average of the two weights, such as (m₁g+m₂g)/2, instead of deriving it from the pulley's own force balance, and picking both statements true.
